title: the tester's closure runner puts the proof's own directory first on sys.path, so a proof imports its own checkout whatever the caller's cwd
intention: TesterDevice's _CLOSURE_RUNNER replaces a leading empty sys.path entry with the proof's directory, as running the proof as a script would, so the pinned checkout wins on every host and from every cwd.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: run_proof from cwd=live root printed sys.path[0]=='' and imported the live cairn; test_hollow's worktree tooth red on Windows; with the 4-line edit sys.path[0] is the proof dir and that tooth is ok. Linux test_hollow reads 29/29 green (reseal 05:19), so the cwd there is not the live root
traces_to: Law 3: the cause was measured (cwd live root gives the live cairn, cwd proofs dir gives the worktree); Law 8: the proof reds on the unedited runner on any host; CP: a hollow run measures the tree it says it measures.
how: In cairn/devices/tester/device.py _CLOSURE_RUNNER, after sys.argv is set: if sys.path and sys.path[0] == '' then sys.path[0] = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(_proof)). Red-first proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_closure_runner_puts_the_proofs_dir_first.py runs run_proof for real from a foreign cwd, so it reds on Linux too.

clauses.claim: with the caller's cwd set to the live repo root, the probe's sys.path[0] is the proof's own directory
a module beside the proof beats a same-named module in the caller's cwd
